See also: Gallina

Asturian

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Latin gallīna.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ɡaˈʎina/ [ɡaˈʎi.na]
  • Rhymes: -ina
  • Syllabification: ga‧lli‧na

Noun

[edit]

gallina f (plural gallines)

  1. hen (female bird (i.e. chicken))
    Synonym: pita

Catalan

[edit]

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • galina (Mallorca)

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Old Catalan gallina, from Latin gallīna. Compare Occitan galina, Old French jeline, Spanish gallina.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): (Central, Balearic) [ɡəˈʎi.nə]
  • IPA(key): (Valencia) [ɡaˈʎi.na]
  • Audio (Catalonia):(file)
  • Rhymes: -ina

Noun

[edit]

gallina f (plural gallines)

  1. hen

Derived terms

[edit]
  • carn de gallina
  • gallina cega
  • gallinaire
  • gallinassa
  • gallinejar
  • galliner

Adjective

[edit]

gallina m or f (masculine and feminine plural gallines)

  1. cowardly

See also

[edit]
  • lloca

References

[edit]
  • “gallina”, in Diccionari de la llengua catalana [Dictionary of the Catalan Language] (in Catalan), second edition, Institute of Catalan Studies [Catalan: Institut d'Estudis Catalans], April 2007
  • “gallina”, in Gran Diccionari de la Llengua Catalana, Grup Enciclopèdia Catalana, 2026
  • “gallina” in Diccionari normatiu valencià, Acadèmia Valenciana de la Llengua.
  • “gallina” in Diccionari català-valencià-balear, Antoni Maria Alcover and Francesc de Borja Moll, 1962.

Latin

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *gelH-
Proto-Italic *galsos
Latin gallus
Proto-Indo-European *-nós
Proto-Indo-European *-iHnos
Proto-Italic *-īnos
Latin -inus
Latin -īna
Latin gallina

    From gallus (“rooster”) + -īna.

    Pronunciation

    [edit]
    • (Classical Latin) IPA(key): [ɡalˈliː.na]
    • (modern Italianate Ecclesiastical) IPA(key): [ɡalˈliː.na]

    Noun

    [edit]

    gallīna f (genitive gallīnae); first declension

    1. hen (female chicken)
      Anatum ōva gallīnīs saepe suppōnimus.
      We often place the eggs of ducks under hens.

    Declension

    [edit]

    First-declension noun.

    singular plural
    nominative gallīna gallīnae
    genitive gallīnae gallīnārum
    dative gallīnae gallīnīs
    accusative gallīnam gallīnās
    ablative gallīnā gallīnīs
    vocative gallīna gallīnae

    Derived terms

    [edit]
    • gallīnāceus
    • gallīnārium
    • gallīnārius

    Descendants

    [edit]

      • Istro-Romanian: gălirĕ

    • Italo-Dalmatian:
      • Corsican: gallina, ghjaddina, ghjallina
      • Dalmatian: galaina
      • Italian: gallina
      • Sicilian: gaddina, jaddina
      • Venetan: gaƚina
    • Rhaeto-Romance:
      • Friulian: gjaline
      • Ladin: gialina
      • Romansh: giaglina (Rumantsch Grischun), gagliegna, gaglina
    • Gallo-Italic:
      • Lombard: gaina
    • Gallo-Romance:
      • Catalan: gallina
      • Old French: geline
        • French: géline
        • Franc-Comtois: dgelène
        • Norman: gelène
        • Picard: glinne, glaine
          • Amiénois: glangne
      • Old Occitan: galina, galinha
        • Occitan: galina
    • Ibero-Romance:
      • Asturian: gallina
      • Old Galician-Portuguese: galinha
        • Galician: galiña
        • Portuguese: galinha (see there for further descendants)
      • Spanish: gallina
    • Germanic
      • → English: galeny, galeeny

    Spanish

    [edit]

    Etymology

    [edit]

    Inherited from Old Spanish, from Latin gallīna.

    Pronunciation

    [edit]
     
    • IPA(key): /ɡaˈʝina/ [ɡaˈʝi.na]
    • IPA(key): /ɡaˈʝina/ [ɡaˈʝi.na] (Equatorial Guinea, most of Spain and Latin America)
    • IPA(key): /ɡaˈʎina/ [ɡaˈʎi.na] (rural northern Spain, Andes Mountains, Paraguay, Philippines)
    • IPA(key): /ɡaˈʃina/ [ɡaˈʃi.na] (Buenos Aires and environs)
    • IPA(key): /ɡaˈʒina/ [ɡaˈʒi.na] (elsewhere in Argentina and Uruguay)

    • Rhymes: -ina
    • Syllabification: ga‧lli‧na

    Noun

    [edit]

    gallina f (plural gallinas, masculine gallo, masculine plural gallos)

    1. hen
    2. (colloquial) chicken (coward)
      Synonyms: cagado, cagón, cagueta, cobarde
      • 2022, Pedro Arizpe, Puerto Jerez‎[1] (webcomic):
        ¡Ya pues, no te asomes! Queda claro que eres bien gallina...
        Okay, fine! Don't look outside. It's clear you're a big chicken...
